subject.title: Memory system: Cannot delete stale memories, conflicting entries persist

question: Should OpenClaw first fix the narrow `memory_recall` to `memory_forget(memoryId=...)` selector handoff, or fold this entire stale-memory cleanup report into the broader memory lifecycle contract?
rationale: Current source proves the selector gap, but the issue also asks for replacement/deprecation semantics that affect durable memory lifecycle, storage, privacy, and plugin API behavior.

options.title: Split narrow fix from lifecycle design
options.body: Expose deletable UUIDs in model-visible `memory_recall` output now, and leave replacement, tombstone, and conflict-resolution semantics to the broader Memory MVP tracker.

options.title: Fold into Memory MVP only
options.body: Treat this report as a concrete reproduction for the broader lifecycle work and do not land a standalone LanceDB selector repair until the full contract is chosen.

options.title: Defer pending live repro
options.body: Keep the issue blocked until a maintainer or contributor reproduces the exact forget-by-query miss against a real LanceDB and embedding setup.

recommendation.title: Split narrow fix from lifecycle design
recommendation.body: Expose deletable UUIDs in model-visible `memory_recall` output now, and leave replacement, tombstone, and conflict-resolution semantics to the broader Memory MVP tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical Memory MVP review and recent memory storage history make this the best available owner for the lifecycle/API decision.
